provenance.abstraction_rationale: The report links a segmentation fault to torch.nn.functional.cosine_embedding_loss input handling. The associated PR patch and comment indicate that only input1's dimensionality was checked before the target-dimension branch, allowing mismatched input1 and input2 shapes to proceed to a crashing code path.

historical_conditions.statement: A reproducer called torch.nn.functional.cosine_embedding_loss with input1 as an empty (0, 0) float16 tensor, input2 as an empty (0,) int8 tensor, and target as an empty (0,) float32 tensor.

The two input tensors had different dimensionalities/shapes: input1 was 2D while input2 was 1D, which the linked documentation describes as not allowed for CosineEmbeddingLoss and which was not checked in the code.

defect_mechanism.description: The native cosine_embedding_loss implementation only validated input1.dim() in the target-dimension branches. With a 1D target, input1 having dim 2 passed the existing check while input2 having dim 1 was not rejected, so execution continued into a code path that produced a segmentation fault.

observed_failure.description: The call emitted a deprecation warning and then terminated with 'Segmentation fault (core dumped)'.

historical_observations.statement: A commenter reproduced the crash on nightly and marked it high priority.
The associated PR added tests expecting RuntimeError rather than a crash for mismatched input shapes.
